notes: Hook: sound. Work done by an expanding gas is in the research (SQA HN unit, R12) and the pressure of a gas expanding as pV^n = C (n > 0) does keep falling, so a single force times distance will not do; it matches i9.

oneBreath: 'one rule for powers finds most of them' overclaims. The power rule finds the derivatives of powers and polynomials, not of sines, exponentials or logarithms, and no source says it covers most derivatives. Suggest 'one rule for powers finds the ones this course uses' or 'one rule finds the derivative of any power'.

oneBreath: 'the same rule run backwards gets it exactly, right through to mean and RMS values' overclaims. The reversed power rule gives exact totals for powers, but the course's RMS of a sine wave (peak / sqrt 2, i10) is not got from the power rule. Suggest 'and the reverse of differentiating gets it exactly, right through to mean and RMS values'.

oneBreath: the rest is sound: two halves that undo each other (R5), derivative as a rate at an instant with current as the rate charge flows (i2, i5), a zero slope at a largest or smallest value of a smooth curve (i6), integral as a total such as charge from current or work from a pV diagram (i8, i9, R12).
